H4SC01313.name: Sheri Biggs
H4SC01313.bio: Air National Guard lieutenant colonel and board-certified family and psychiatric mental health nurse practitioner seeking re-election in South Carolina's Third District.

positions.stance: Will work to build the wall, stop the flow of illegal aliens and drugs, and replace "catch-and-release" with "stop-and-deport."
Will fight for "fiscal responsibility, accountability, and transparency" of taxpayer dollars, citing excessive spending that fueled inflation and debt.
Believes all life is made in God's image and will use her voice to "protect the sanctity of life and advance a true culture of life."
Says the nation needs more political outsiders to prioritize the people's issues and "return the power to the American people."
Will fight to ensure those who served receive "the honor, dignity, respect, and care they deserve."

H6SC03090.name: Eunice Lehmacher
H6SC03090.bio: Licensed professional counselor in Oconee and Pickens counties since 2002 and former private-practice owner, hospital social worker and Clemson University student counselor.

positions.stance: Wants to make housing, groceries, utilities, child care, college and other necessities more affordable, and to rein in tariffs.
Supports lowering utility costs "by investing in cheaper, cleaner energy" and investing in parks, trails, roads, bridges and infrastructure.
Calls to stop funding masked ICE agents, stop costly wars, and defend First and Second Amendment rights against government threats.
Calls healthcare "a basic human need and human right"; supports reducing insurance and drug costs and restoring Medicare, Medicaid and ACA funding.
Supports stopping mass deportation of law-abiding undocumented immigrants and resuming asylum-law processes, alongside a balance of enforcement and reform.

H8SC04250.name: William Timmons
H8SC04250.bio: U.S. Representative for South Carolina's 4th District since 2019; attorney, former prosecutor, small business owner and Air National Guard JAG officer.

positions.stance: Says he has stood with President Trump and will "continue fighting for the America First agenda in Congress."
Fighting to lower costs, cut wasteful spending and "unleash American energy production" to stop inflation hurting working families.
Will keep fighting to finish the border wall, end catch-and-release, stop fentanyl and deport criminal illegal immigrants.
Supports law enforcement and opposes efforts "to defund the police and weaken public safety."
"I am proudly pro-life"; supports policies that defend the unborn and opposes expanding taxpayer-funded abortion.

H6SC04171.name: Courtney McClain
H6SC04171.bio: Civil rights advocate and former president of the South Carolina NAACP Youth and College Division, with a master's in political science from Howard University.

positions.stance: Would restrict corporate landlords and private equity firms from buying single-family homes and remove large buyers' tax advantages over individual homebuyers.
Supports fully funding the ACA, increasing subsidies, and expanding Medicare and supporting Medicare for All.
Would ban dynamic pricing for groceries, rent and necessities and regulate when companies can change their prices.
Supports federal funding for public transit and grid upgrades and a moratorium on building new AI data centers.
Supports a national teacher pay incentive program, universal free school meals for children in need, and increased Title I funding.

H6SC05202.name: Wes Climer
H6SC05202.bio: Financial advisor and business owner representing York County in the South Carolina State Senate.

positions.stance: Filed a lawsuit against a legislative pay raise and will "fight to expose corruption and force transparency on every dime spent."
Supports President Trump and will advance the America First agenda on immigration, energy, national security and the rule of law.
Supports building the wall, reinstating Remain in Mexico, defunding sanctuary cities, and stopping fentanyl and human trafficking.
Supports parental rights, eliminating "woke curriculum," and abolishing the federal Department of Education entirely.
Will vote to slash spending, block tax hikes, and restore federalism by returning power to states and citizens.

H6SC05228.name: Mallory Dittmer
H6SC05228.bio: Former vice president in the corporate retail industry who spent 15 years building partnerships with American fashion brands.

positions.stance: Running "to bring costs down, wages up"; supports lowering grocery, utility, child care and housing costs and raising the $7.25 minimum wage.
Supports lowering premiums and drug costs, improving the ACA, reversing cuts to ACA subsidies, Medicare and Medicaid, and saving rural hospitals.
Will fight to fully fund public schools, keep public funds in public schools, expand pre-k, and re-establish the federal Department of Education.
Supports safe digital spaces for kids, firearm education and secure storage, and federal grants for youth programs to prevent juvenile crime.
Supports strengthening alliances including NATO through diplomacy, ending endless wars, and upholding constitutional checks and balances.

H2SC02042.name: Jim Clyburn
H2SC02042.bio: Congressman for South Carolina's Sixth District since 1993; former public school teacher and South Carolina Human Affairs Commissioner.

positions.stance: His 10-20-30 plan directs at least 10 percent of funds to persistently poor communities; he is working to make it permanent law.
Working to expand the Rural Energy Savings Program and develop a similar program to make broadband more available in rural communities.
Developing a third South Carolina Heritage Corridor and working to ensure the state gets its fair share of the tourism economy.
Backs a bill allowing up to $50,000 in student loan cancellation for people earning under $100,000.
Committed to ensuring "all eligible Americans have the right to cast a ballot that is counted"; supports reinstating Voting Rights Act preclearance.

H6SC06184.name: John Peterson
H6SC06184.bio: Banquet supervisor for Embassy Suites at the North Charleston Convention Center and Charleston County Republican Party precinct president.

positions.stance: Will "Support the Trump agenda and Prevent the Democrats from impeaching President Trump."
Will vote for fiscally conservative bills "that cut spending, reduce inflation, and bring down the national debt."
Will champion tough-on-crime bills "that protect law abiding citizens and keep violent criminals off the street."
Will "Fight for Free and Fair Elections that require Voter I.D."
Supports DOGE and will work "to uncover Fraud Waste and Abuse" of taxpayer dollars.

H2SC07280.name: Russell Fry
H2SC07280.bio: Congressman for South Carolina's Seventh District, former Grand Strand attorney, and former Horry County state representative and State House Chief Majority Whip.

positions.stance: Will fight to lock in the America First agenda and back the President's judges and nominees.
Supports finishing the wall, ending catch-and-release, deporting criminal illegal aliens, and destroying "the fentanyl pipeline."
Supports making the Trump tax cuts permanent, rolling back regulations on small businesses and farmers, and cutting wasteful federal spending.
Calls the Chinese Communist Party "the greatest long-term threat to America"; supports reshoring supply chains and blocking adversary farmland purchases.
Pledges to protect religious freedom, "Defend the Second Amendment without compromise," and "Stand for life."

H6SC07034.name: John Vincent
H6SC07034.bio: U.S. Navy career veteran and retired Command Master Chief, former Gallup leadership development consultant, and small business owner.

positions.stance: Would work to pass the War Powers Resolution so Congress can "reel in this unconstitutional war" in Iran.
Would work with all members of Congress "to end global tariffs," citing harm to farmers and small business owners.
Would introduce legislation to remove the Social Security income cap, which he says would add 30 years of solvency.
Pushing to pass the Major Richard Star Act, Caring for Survivors Act, and Supporting Families in Need Act.
Plans to introduce an ALL American Healthcare Act offering low-cost insurance and a Fiscal Responsibility and Debt Stabilization Act to control spending.

H6SC89016.name: Joseph Madge
H6SC89016.bio: Manufacturing engineer with over 30 years of experience and former chair of the Lexington County Democratic Party.

positions.stance: Supports teacher retention, practical curriculum for trade-bound students, and stronger vocational training for workforce readiness.
Supports investing in public transportation and prioritizing critical road and bridge repairs across District 89.

positions.topic: Cost of living and health care
positions.stance: Supports expanding affordable housing, childcare and paid leave, expanding Medicaid, and cutting taxes for middle-class residents.
Supports defending workers' rights, investing in manufacturing, clean energy and research, and protecting family farms and small businesses.
Supports clean energy investment, data-driven pollution regulations, and holding "corporate polluters financially responsible for their impact."

H0AL01055.name: Jerry Carl
H0AL01055.bio: Mobile businessman who has started more than ten companies, a former Mobile County commissioner, and a former member of Congress.

positions.stance: Will "continue to work alongside President Trump to make our country safer, stronger, and more prosperous."
Calls illegal immigration "a direct threat to our national security"; backed border wall funding and record Border Patrol hiring.
A lifelong Second Amendment supporter who "will defend our right to bear and keep arms."
Has "led the charge to protect women's sports" and pledges to keep men out of women's sports.
Believes parents should be in charge of their children's education and wants to keep "critical race theory and woke ideology out of the classroom."

H6AL01094.name: Clyde Jones
H6AL01094.bio: Retired Army first sergeant and Bronze Star recipient, former FMC Corporation process safety management coordinator, and associate minister.

positions.stance: "I believe in the expansion of Medicaid, and ACA Enhanced Premium Tax Credits"; supports a direct federal coverage program in non-expansion states.
Will work to restore constitutional checks and balances "and ensure Americans aren't governed by executive orders."
Will vote to overturn Citizens United, ban stock trading by members and their families, and support term limits and a lobbying moratorium.
Will fight for "a clear, straightforward path for undocumented people to get documented" while saying secure borders are important.
Supports "a moratorium on building new data centers" until adequate environmental impact investigations are conducted.

H4AL02170.name: Shomari Figures
H4AL02170.bio: U.S. Representative for Alabama's 2nd District, a University of Alabama law graduate with prior experience at the U.S. Department of Justice.

positions.stance: Says he fought to protect SNAP and Social Security benefits and delivered funding for job training programs.
Pushed to expand Medicaid in Alabama, introduced legislation to help rural hospitals stay open, and "Defended reproductive rights and patient decision-making."
Introduced legislation for a first-time parent tax credit and to exempt baby items like cribs, bassinets and baby monitors from tariffs.
Introduced legislation for a "$15 billion tariff relief program for small and mid-sized farmers."
Supported capping student loan interest rates and introduced legislation covering college costs for children of first responders, teachers and social workers.

H6AL01086.name: Rhett Marques
H6AL01086.bio: Small business owner who ran a tire and automotive service business in Enterprise for over 26 years and has served in the Alabama Legislature.

positions.stance: Calls affordability his top priority; will "fight to eliminate wasteful spending, lower taxes, and put more of your hard-earned money back in your pocket."
Will "slash job-strangling red tape" and work to onshore critical supply chains and raise real wages.
Pledges to make Washington as veteran-friendly as he says Alabama has become.
Supports "Detain and Deport" in place of "Catch and Release" and will fight to keep criminal illegal aliens out of communities.
Will work for fair markets for producers and invest in broadband and infrastructure for rural healthcare, education and opportunity.

H2AL03032.name: Mike Rogers
H2AL03032.bio: Chairman of the House Armed Services Committee; former Anniston attorney and businessman, Calhoun County commissioner, and Alabama House Minority Leader.

H6AL03199.name: Lee McInnis
H6AL03199.bio: Army Intelligence veteran who spent 28 years in the Defense Intelligence Community, later teaching communications and American government.

positions.stance: Says the economy must work for everyone and pledges to "level the field for working families, and make life affordable for all of us."
Cites healthcare deserts in the district and says "We can have healthcare for all."
Will accept no money from corporate PACs or foreign-government PACs and will hold town hall meetings so everyone can hold him accountable.

H6AL04098.name: Robert Aderholt
H6AL04098.bio: U.S. Representative for Alabama's Fourth District serving his 15th term, member of the House Appropriations Committee, and former Haleyville municipal judge.

positions.stance: Calls rebuilding the economy his top priority; working to cut taxes, slash regulation, bring jobs back, and expand energy production.
Supports bolstering the defense budget, modernizing military capabilities, advancing cyber defenses, and maintaining U.S. superiority in space.
Believes in the constitutional right to bear arms and opposes firearm confiscation and expanded gun control legislation.
Opposes defunding police; supports training and hiring programs, improved de-escalation protocols, and reformed data collection.
Condemns Russia's invasion of Ukraine, supports stopping U.S. purchases of Russian oil and gas, and wants NATO members spending at least 2% of GDP on defense.

H6AL05228.name: Amanda Pusczek
H6AL05228.bio: Registered nurse with over a decade of frontline clinical experience in hospitals, clinics, schools and correctional facilities.

positions.stance: Proposes a federal relief fund of non-repayable grants to keep rural and Critical Access Hospitals open and reversing cuts to Medicaid safety-net payments.
Supports raising the federal minimum wage to $15.00, passing the PRO Act, and a constitutional amendment to overturn Citizens United.
Supports zero-tolerance federal limits on PFAS chemicals in public water and holding corporate polluters financially accountable.
Supports passing the John Lewis Voting Rights Advancement Act and reinstating federal preclearance requirements.
Supports expanding local veteran healthcare networks, eliminating claim backlogs, and establishing specialized mental health triage for veterans.

H2AL05102.name: Dale Strong
H2AL05102.bio: Former volunteer firefighter and paramedic who served as a district commissioner and Chairman of the Madison County Commission.

positions.stance: "I am a pro-life Christian who will stand up for the unborn and fight for our Christian values."
Says he is running so the Trump movement continues, calling Conservative control of the House "JOB ONE."
"Raising taxes is not an option"; says cutting wasteful spending and downsizing government must be a top priority.
Opposes "defund the police" and pledges to ensure officers have the support and equipment to protect families.
"I fully support building the wall, sending illegals back to their country of origin, and fully enforcing the law."

H6AL05244.name: Andrew Sneed
H6AL05244.bio: Master plumber and gas fitter who founded and operates the Huntsville small business Whole Home Solutions.

positions.stance: Supports expanding Medicaid availability, negotiating prescription drug costs, and regulating for-profit insurance companies.
Supports comprehensive reform including legal frameworks for undocumented immigrants already working in the U.S. and making ICE "regulated and accountable."
Supports expanding rental assistance and affordable housing, repealing "unjustified tariffs," and restoring federal investment in energy efficiency.
Supports fast-track training for high-demand trades, worker safety protections, and the right to collective bargaining.

H4AL06098.name: Gary Palmer
H4AL06098.bio: U.S. Representative for Alabama's 6th District since 2015 and founder and former president of the Alabama Policy Institute.

positions.stance: Believes the First Amendment guarantees the freedom to live and work according to one's faith "without government coercion."
Supports responsibly developing America's energy resources and reining in EPA regulatory overreach, including through his Stopping EPA Overreach Act.
Believes honoring veterans means respecting their service and supporting them when they return home.
Supports "a strong, well-funded military" and backed the National Defense Authorization Act.
Believes fiscal responsibility "starts with living within our means" and pushes to address waste, fraud and improper payments.

H6AL06184.name: Maurice Mercer
H6AL06184.bio: Account executive for a Fortune 500 company and former three-term Pelham City Council member and council president.

positions.stance: Will fight for policies that "lower costs, increase competition, strengthen supply chains, and help working families keep more of what they earn."
Supports expanding affordable healthcare, protecting rural providers, improving mental health services, and prescription drug price transparency.
Supports a woman's right to make her own healthcare decisions while backing efforts to strengthen families and reduce adoption barriers.
Supports excellent public schools, expanded career and technical education, apprenticeships, and improved broadband for students.
Will work to reduce unnecessary regulations, expand access to capital, and improve broadband for entrepreneurs.

H0AL07086.name: Terri Sewell
H0AL07086.bio: Congresswoman for Alabama's 7th District and former public finance lawyer.

positions.stance: Fighting to lower costs of everyday essentials; advocates lowering prescription drug prices and strengthening nutrition assistance, and opposes Trump's tariffs.
Supports expanding Medicaid in Alabama and authored the Bridge to Medicaid Act for people in the coverage gap.
Believes "protecting voting rights is the key to building a stronger democracy"; opposes voter suppression and gerrymandering.
Has fought to rebuild roads and bridges, fix water and sewer systems, and ensure every Alabamian has high-speed internet.
Introduced legislation to close tax loopholes that divert money from public schools to private academies.

H6AL07208.name: Ammie Akin
H6AL07208.bio: Entrepreneur and educator with a doctorate in educational leadership who has worked as a special-needs teacher, principal trainer and nonprofit co-founder.

positions.stance: Wants strong communities where families can afford to live, children get a quality education, and neighborhoods have infrastructure and opportunity.
Would tackle rising housing, grocery, utility, transportation and childcare costs "through responsible federal spending and less unnecessary regulation."
Supports small businesses and strong local economies "that create real opportunities for working families."
Would strengthen education through cooperation among teachers, parents, school leaders and communities.
Wants to prepare every student to succeed, "whether their path leads to college, a career, or another opportunity after high school."

H0LA01087.name: Steve Scalise
H0LA01087.bio: House Majority Leader representing Louisiana's 1st District since 2008, former state legislator and former software engineer.

positions.stance: Has "always exercised fiscal discipline, pushed for lower taxes, and believed in balancing our nation's checkbook."
Committed to "fighting for secure borders" and undoing what he calls the Biden administration's pro-amnesty policies.
Will fight for a national energy strategy that enhances production, streamlines permitting, and reduces dependence on China and other foreign nations.
Believes in "protecting and promoting parents' role in their child's education."
Believes in "standing up for pro-life values, and protecting the Second Amendment rights of law-abiding citizens."

H6LA01258.name: Lauren Jewett
H6LA01258.bio: National Board Certified special education teacher with 17 years in Louisiana schools and a union member.

positions.stance: Supports more oversight of insurance companies and federal action "to cap annual insurance rate increases."
Would protect Social Security from cuts, reject privatization, and adjust the payroll tax cap so higher earners pay at the same rate.
Will "fight to fully fund federal special education law" (IDEA) and keep it at the Department of Education.
Opposes executive overreach, supports overturning Citizens United, and backs term limits for members of Congress.
Would co-sponsor the John Lewis Voting Rights Advancement Act and Freedom to Vote Act and opposes the SAVE America Act.

H2LA02149.name: Troy Carter
H2LA02149.bio: U.S. Representative for Louisiana's 2nd District serving his third term; former Louisiana state senator, state representative and New Orleans City Council member.

positions.stance: Will fight for Louisianians to live the "American Dream" by creating equal and fair housing legislation.
Will "Continue the fight for our citizens who are living with disabilities."
Will fight for "criminal justice reform, environmental justice, equal pay and a living wage for all Louisianians."
Will advocate for the "reduction or elimination of student loan debt."
Will champion letting women "make 100% of the decisions concerning their health and reproductive rights."
